description: Public status page for solar-control: periodic instance-state sampling into a history table, a public status-summary endpoint (current availability + 90-day uptime per virtual model / alias / non-managed instance, intent phases), maintainer status messages with automatic visibility windows, a 5-year retention job, and the solar-status SPA rendering the standard status-page layout (component status, 90-day uptime bars, active and upcoming messages). Out of scope: notification/subscription features, incident post-mortems, per-endpoint metrics UI, changes to gateway routing or the existing /webui dashboard, programmatic message control. Reads are public and unauthenticated; writes sit behind the existing management key.

userStories.title: State-history table and data access layer
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a Postgres table that logs instance states over time so availability and uptime history can be computed even without request traffic.
acceptanceCriteria: New instance-state-history SQLAlchemy row in app/database/tables.py with columns: id, alias, instance_id, host_id, state, sampled_at (timestamptz)
Indexes support the summary query pattern: filter by alias/instance_id over a sampled_at window (90 days) and efficient cleanup by sampled_at
Alembic migration generated under app/database/migrations/versions/ and `alembic upgrade head` succeeds
A StateHistoryDB class in app/database/ provides batch insert and windowed-read helpers, following the existing *DB singleton pattern (e.g. virtual_model_db in app/database/virtual_models.py)
make test-solar-control passes and make lint-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: Table instance_state_history (migration 0012) and StateHistoryDB (insert_batch, read_window) in app/database/state_history.py; migration verified up/down against a throwaway Postgres.

userStories.title: Instance-state sampler background loop
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a periodic sampler that records the current state of every registered instance so history accumulates continuously, including during requestless outages.
acceptanceCriteria: Sampler service modeled after the Reconciler background-loop pattern (app/services/reconciliation.py): asyncio.create_task in start(), stop() cancels and awaits the task, loop sleep driven by an asyncio.Event with timeout
Started and stopped in the app/main.py lifespan alongside the existing background jobs

Each tick reads RegistryStore.get_registry (app/redis_state/registry.py) and the WS-first host snapshots (solar:hosts:snapshots via app/redis_state/hosts.py, freshness via entry_age_s) and writes one sample row per instance: alias, instance_id, host_id, state, sampled_at
Instance state derived from the host snapshot health/status (e.g. running/offline); alias taken from registry membership; stale or missing snapshots do not crash the loop
Sampling interval configurable via app/config.py Settings
Unit tests cover sampler behavior: one row per instance per tick, state values, empty-registry and stale-snapshot handling
make test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: StateSampler in app/services/state_sampler.py (state_sampler singleton), started/stopped in the lifespan. Interval: Settings.state_sample_interval_s (30s). A Redis NX lock (0.9 x interval) lets one replica sample per interval. State is running when the host's WS resource snapshot is fresh (host_snapshot_max_age_s), else offline; instances absent from the registry get no row.

userStories.title: Public status summary endpoint
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want a public endpoint returning current availability and 90-day uptime per component so the status page can render without any authentication.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/status (app/routes/management/status.py) returns the summary JSON instead of the current 501 placeholder

Endpoint is public: reachable without X-API-Key/Bearer by adding a narrow exemption for this route in the auth middleware (app/auth.py), while all other /api/* routes keep requiring the management key

Response covers, per virtual model (with its ordered targets and target_status semantics: satisfied / violating: <reason> / missing, reusing the computation on VirtualModelResponse.target_status), per alias (core, wind), and per non-managed instance: current availability based on instance states

90-day uptime percentage per component computed from state-history samples in 1d buckets using the resolve_bucket/fill_buckets ladder in app/database/logs.py; zero-filled gaps for outages, never interpolated over
Uptime is computed from the state-history samples, not gateway_requests (a requestless outage still counts as downtime)
Intent-managed model groups surface their reconciliation phase (ready / degraded / failed) alongside availability, sourced from the intents table phase
Unit tests cover uptime math (gap-free series, outage handling) and the response shape
make test-solar-control passes and make lint-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: If model-name disclosure is ever a concern, the keyed-detail variant is the documented fallback shape; ship public by default.

userStories.title: Status messages table and management CRUD
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want to create, list, update and delete status messages via the management API so I can communicate incidents and maintenance to users.
acceptanceCriteria: New status_messages table (body, type: incident | maintenance | planned maintenance | resolution, start_time, end_time optional/open-ended, created_at) plus Alembic migration
CRUD routes under the /api management router (include_router in app/routes/management/__init__.py), following the virtual-models CRUD pattern (POST returns 201, list, PUT, DELETE)
Routes are guarded by the existing management-key auth (X-API-Key / Bearer) via the middleware - no per-route dependency wiring
Validation: type restricted to the allowed set; start_time must not be after end_time when both are set
Unit tests cover CRUD happy path and validation errors
make test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: Messages are always written by a maintainer - no programmatic message control.

userStories.title: Automatic message visibility window
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want messages to appear and expire automatically based on their start/end times so maintainers never have to manually publish or unpublish them.
acceptanceCriteria: Public, unauthenticated message read (included in the GET /api/status response) returns active messages (start_time <= now < end_time)
Messages with a past end_time are filtered from the public read automatically for all types

Planned-maintenance messages with a future start_time are exposed as upcoming so a planned weekend maintenance can be published in advance; other types (incident, maintenance, resolution) follow the strict window and are filtered while their start_time is in the future
No manual publish/unpublish state: visibility is derived purely from start_time/end_time
Unit tests cover the start/end boundary filtering for each message type
make test-solar-control passes
userStories.notes: plan.md states messages with a future start time are filtered from the public read, but also requires planned maintenance to be publishable in advance and the page to show upcoming maintenance. Reconciled as: only planned-maintenance messages surface ahead of their start_time (as upcoming); all other types are strictly window-filtered.

userStories.title: Status page: component status and 90-day uptime bars
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to see each component's current status and its 90-day uptime history at a glance so I can assess the health of the system.
acceptanceCriteria: solar-status (+page.svelte) is replaced with the status page: it fetches GET /api/status through the existing fetchJson client (src/lib/api/client.ts) and renders the standard status-page layout
Component list covering virtual models, aliases (core, wind) and non-managed instances with a colored current-status indicator (operational / degraded / down, plus intent phase where surfaced)
90-day uptime bar per component: one bar per 1d bucket from the gap-free series, outage days rendered as zero/failure-colored gaps, never interpolated
Uptime percentage over the last 90 days displayed per component
Loading, API-unreachable and empty states are handled gracefully; no management key is needed for any read
Component tests (vitest + @testing-library/svelte) cover the rendering states; pnpm --filter solar-status check passes; make test-solar-status and make lint-solar-status pass
Verify both serving modes: make dev-status (cross-origin dev) and embedded mode (pnpm --filter solar-status build, then make dev-control and open /status)

userStories.title: Status page: active and upcoming messages
userStories.description: As a visitor, I want to see active incidents and upcoming maintenance on the status page so I know about current problems and planned downtime.
acceptanceCriteria: Messages section renders active messages from the public read: body, type and window (start/end)
Planned-maintenance messages ahead of their start_time render in an upcoming section
Type-styled badges distinguish incident / maintenance / planned maintenance / resolution
Empty state shown when there are no messages
Component tests cover the message rendering and empty state; pnpm --filter solar-status check passes; make test-solar-status passes

userStories.title: 5-year retention cleanup job
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a daily cleanup job that deletes state-history rows older than 5 years so the history table stays bounded without losing the last 5 years of data.
acceptanceCriteria: Daily background job started in the app/main.py lifespan, following the existing background-loop pattern, deleting state-history rows with sampled_at older than 5 years
Retention window and run interval configurable via app/config.py Settings
Unit test covers the retention boundary: rows just inside the 5-year window are kept, rows beyond it are deleted
make test-solar-control passes
